name: Amina Hassan
description: New resident from Sudan starting over in the UK — navigating NI number, Universal Credit, eVisa transition, and school place for son

amina.qualification: Bachelor of Pharmacy, University of Khartoum (2014)
amina.notes: Pharmacy degree not yet recognised by GPhC. Needs to apply for overseas pharmacist assessment.

financials.notes: Receiving £49.18/week asylum support (Section 95). No bank account — receives support via Aspen card. No NI number yet.

children.notes: Age 6, born in Sudan. Needs school place. Some English from nursery in dispersal accommodation.

family.notes: Single mother. Husband killed in conflict in Sudan 2022. No family in UK. Small community of Sudanese women in Bradford dispersal accommodation.

housing.propertyType: Shared house — single room with Yusuf
housing.notes: Must find own accommodation within 28 days of refugee status grant. Section 95 support ends.

communicationStyle.tone: Polite and formal. Sometimes hesitant — searching for the right English word. Determined but overwhelmed by the number of things to do. Protective of Yusuf's needs above her own.
communicationStyle.techSavvy: Intermediate — uses WhatsApp and Google Translate regularly. Can navigate basic websites but struggles with long government forms in English. Uses phone for everything, no laptop.
primaryConcerns: Getting an NI number so she can work and claim benefits
Finding a school place for Yusuf
Understanding the BRP to eVisa transition before expiry
Opening a bank account with no proof of address history
Finding stable housing before Section 95 support ends
Getting her pharmacy qualification recognised in the UK
typicalPhrases: I just got my refugee status. What do I need to do?
I have my BRP but they say it is changing to eVisa — I don't understand.
My son Yusuf needs a school. He is six and has not been to school here.
I was a pharmacist in Sudan. I want to work but I don't have a National Insurance number.
They gave me a letter but I don't understand all the words.
I don't have a bank account. How can I receive money?

logins.notes: Created a GOV.UK One Login for her eVisa and Universal Credit, and proved her identity at a Post Office. No Government Gateway — she has never dealt with HMRC. Finds the whole thing bewildering in a second language.
